title: Astra Microwave Products Ltd - 532493 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Astra Microwave won a ~Rs 2,205 crore HAL Uttam radar order, lifting order book to ~Rs 4,300 crore, while Q1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 182 crore.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was Rs 182 crore against new Q1 orders of Rs 185 crore, which management said matched its guidance. Management attributed the quarter's weak revenue to delayed programs caused by inspection and specification-proof issues and supply-chain gaps, which it expects to recover in Q3 and Q4. The late-July receipt of the HAL Uttam radar order (about Rs 1,870 crore excluding GST, stated as Rs 2,205 crore including GST in the call) more than doubled the order book. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of about Rs 1,350 crore (plus or minus 25%) and said the space and weather businesses will be spun off as a separate listed entity from April 1, 2027.

financial_highlights.metric: Total order book (as of call date)
financial_highlights.change: Roughly doubled after HAL Uttam radar order

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 2,205 crore (about Rs 1,870 crore excluding GST, per management)
66% defence, 34% commercial/services (about Rs 244 crore, typically higher in July)

financial_highlights.change: Attributed to positive cash balance at end FY26 reducing borrowing cost

segments.name: Defence electronics (radar, EW, subsystems)
segments.commentary: Q1 deliveries included CAR, 5G isolation, RoE-Ni and MPR modules, plus Shikthi and NIN EW programmes. A Rs 45 crore Bharat Electronics order for MMIC chipsets was won in the quarter.

segments.name: Space and meteorology (to be spun off)
segments.commentary: Management guided Rs 300+ crore revenue for the standalone space and weather entity in year one at 18-20% PBT margin. About Rs 1,250 crore of the Rs 1,350 crore FY27 project sales is stated to come from the space sector, and about 150 crore of run-rate business was cited. Doppler weather radar supplies to IMD exceed 45 units over four years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of Rs 1,350 crore plus or minus 25%; FY28 about Rs 1,600 crore plus or minus 50, with a different trajectory from FY29.

Management said it is targeting top-line growth of more than 15% in FY27 while maintaining a healthy bottom line; the call contained conflicting growth ranges (10-15% in the press release versus 15-20% in the presentation, as raised by an analyst).
Order intake guidance of about Rs 1,600 crore for FY27 was reaffirmed; management said it may be improved over the next few quarters.
Order intake of Rs 8,000-9,000 crore expected over the next 3-4 years, to be executed over 5-6 years; this is an upgrade from the earlier QIP commitment of Rs 8,000-10,000 crore over five years.
Management expects revenue to be about 6-7 times FY26 turnover (Rs 1,057 crore combined) within five years, and Rs 600 million-1 billion annual revenue later.
Margins expected to be similar to last year in the standalone business, with no firm long-term margin guidance given.
Space and weather entity to operate independently from April 1, 2027, with a planned satellite launch within six months of listing.
capex_capacity: HAL Uttam radar: Phase 1 of 12 units to be completed by September 2027, about 14 months from order; about 25 units per year thereafter; management said it may execute the full quantity by FY31.

Two complete indigenous radars and one drone-mounted electronic intelligence product targeted around Diwali 2026; technology demonstrations were held in Jalandhar in July for an electromagnetic wall and a vehicle-mounted anti-drone system.
Management said production lines and teams are fully ready; migration to SAP HANA completed; automated process engineering invested in.
Supply-chain risk flagged for cross-border components, as global nations restock armaments.
demand_pricing: Upcoming order pipeline per management: QRSAM about Rs 7,800 crore (first three regiments), Su-30 and Angad about Rs 3,000 crore, ASSL/SNFL/JV about Rs 500-750 crore; total Rs 8,000-9,000 crore. Management said chip sales, counter-UAV, electromagnetic wall, area denial systems and exports are excluded.
AMCA: Astra was named L1 for radar in a development tender; numbers not disclosed. Tejas Mk1A EW and other programmes add about Rs 500-600 crore to projections.
BrahMos RF seeker and components are in supply, and the BrahMos NG seeker is in proactive development (not in order book). Shatrughat and Samakar subsystems expected to yield about Rs 100-120 crore.
Export: BTS orders executed, MMIC component leads from US and Europe, with sizable orders expected in about two years. Complete counter-drone solutions for exports are expected in one to two years.
Solution pricing is competitive per global feedback, but management declined to commit to margins.

qa_highlights.question: Is top-line growth guidance 10-15% (press release) or 15-20% (presentation), and what are the order book targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not clearly resolve the discrepancy in the answer given. It said the FY27 order intake guidance of about Rs 1,600 crore stands.

qa_highlights.question: What is the upside from EW programmes (Pages, Tejas Mk1A EW, LCH) and the counter-drone and EM wall products?
qa_highlights.answer: Pages EW suite under final qualification; Tejas Mk1A EW adds about Rs 500-600 crore to projections; the counter-drone and EM wall products are all upside not in guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp fall in interest cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower borrowing, because a large positive cash balance from end-FY26 meant minimal interest needed; management said equity is an expensive form of capital.

qa_highlights.question: What is the execution timeline and revenue profile for the Uttam radar order?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 of 12 units by September 2027; about 25 units a year thereafter; full quantity possibly by FY31.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect significant change; Q1 and part of Q2 are seasonally weak, with comfort from Q4, and the position may be similar by end-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the Q1 revenue shortfall?
qa_highlights.answer: Some programmes were delayed by inspection issues, specification proof delays, development-cycle issues and supply-chain gaps; management expects recovery in Q3 and Q4.

risks_watch: Q1 revenue of Rs 182 crore leaves heavy back-end loading for FY27 guidance of Rs 1,350 crore; Q3 and Q4 execution is critical.
Execution capacity for a 6-7x revenue scale-up in five years; management said execution is what keeps it awake at night.
Supply-chain risk for cross-border components, as global armaments restocking increases demand.

Ambiguity in the growth guidance (10-15% versus 15-20%) and the order intake scale (cumulative revenue projections versus order intake), which an analyst flagged and management did not fully reconcile.
Spin-off of space and weather business from April 1, 2027; segment financials and capital allocation remain to be disclosed.
Upcoming AMCA and Diwali-timed product launches are not in the numbers and remain uncertain.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on order wins and long-term growth, but evasive on specifics. Management declined to commit to margins, long-term revenue split or the growth-range discrepancy, and it deferred detail on space to later quarters. The tone on the Q1 shortfall was defensive, attributing it to timing.

Aizan Redd is the single largest order in the history of Astra
I would seriously insist that we look at our ability to deliver our year end revenue targets to you 1350 crores for the current year plus minus 25.
we don't want to commit to you on the margins because there are a lot of factors which will come into play from incremental products

adds.what: HAL Uttam radar Phase 1 production of 12 units (about 25 units per year thereafter)
Two complete indigenous radars and one drone-mounted electronic intelligence product (demonstration/product launch around Diwali 2026)

growth.why: Management targets FY27 revenue of about Rs 1,350 crore (±25%) and said top-line growth of more than 15%, though the call cited conflicting ranges (10-15% vs 15-20%); backing is a Rs 4,300 crore order book after the ~Rs 2,205 crore HAL Uttam order, with Phase 1 of 12 units due by September 2027, but Q1 revenue of Rs 182 crore was weak and recovery is expected only in Q3-Q4.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management said standalone margins will be similar to last year and declined to commit to margins, with solution pricing described as competitive.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: HAL Uttam Phase 1 of 12 units due by September 2027 (about 14 months from order), with about 25 units a year thereafter; production lines said to be fully ready, but the new capacity is for a program delivery rather than a new plant.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue target of about Rs 1,350 crore (plus or minus 25%) needs back-end loading after Q1 revenue of Rs 182 crore, with management expecting delayed programmes to recover in Q3 and Q4.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q1 revenue of Rs 182 crore is weak against the Rs 1,350 crore FY27 target, and management reaffirmed rather than raised guidance, with the growth range (10-15% vs 15-20%) left unresolved.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 revenue of Rs 182 crore is far below a Rs 1,350 crore run-rate, the shortfall was blamed on delays, and the growth range is inconsistent (10-15% vs 15-20%).

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Two complete indigenous radars and one drone-mounted electronic intelligence product are targeted around Diwali 2026, with demonstrations already held in Jalandhar in July.

rows.label: Order pipeline of Rs 8,000-9,000 crore
rows.why: Management lists QRSAM about Rs 7,800 crore, Su-30/Angad about Rs 3,000 crore and ASSL/SNFL/JV about Rs 500-750 crore, but these are pipeline items not yet in the order book, and FY27 order intake of about Rs 1,600 crore was reaffirmed with a Rs 4,300 crore order book after the Rs 2,205 crore Uttam order.

rows.label: Space and weather spin-off from April 1, 2027
rows.why: Separate listed entity guided with Rs 300+ crore first-year revenue at 18-20% PBT margin, and about Rs 1,250 crore of FY27 project sales is space-related; segment financials still to be disclosed.

rows.label: Exports and counter-drone solutions
rows.why: Complete counter-drone solutions for exports are expected in one to two years and MMIC leads from US and Europe have sizable orders expected in about two years, but neither is in the order book or guidance.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Rs 2,205 crore HAL Uttam order and the long-term pipeline but defensive on the Q1 revenue shortfall and evasive on margins and the 10-15% vs 15-20% growth discrepancy, which analysts pressed.

quality.why: Q1 FY27 revenue was Rs 182 crore with no YoY growth figure stated (change listed as "Not stated"), and management attributed the weak quarter to delayed programmes rather than any one-off; the brief gives no volume, price or mix split and no one-off items affecting this quarter's growth.
